text: Supervised fine-tuning is used to elicit UM's self-recognition capability: UM is fine-tuned on the binary classification task of distinguishing UG's code from H's code, then evaluated on a held-out test set. The resulting ROC curve upper-bounds U's passive self-recognition ability, subject to three assumptions: (1) the fine-tuning has converged (verified via checkpoint analysis, Appendix C.4); (2) U cannot perform gradient hacking; (3) the training distribution matches deployment (ensured by online honeypot generation).
title: Self-recognition ROC elicitation assumptions
